# RFC: Pending Model Support — diffusers v0.38+ and Non-diffusers Community Models Not Yet Supported by cache-dit

When to read this: when picking the next model to integrate into cache-dit, or when starting/finishing work on a model listed here (update its Status entry and add a line to R.5). Use R.7 for the unified support-priority queue and R.2/R.6 for implementation difficulty. Return to `../SKILL.md` for the integration workflow; see [`./model_download.md`](./model_download.md) for fetching the weights.

## R.1 Background, Scope and Method

- Analysis dates: **2026-10-22** (three passes: diffusers v0.40+ scan, the v0.38/v0.39 window scan, then unification into one difficulty-ordered list).
- Scope: models **added to diffusers v0.38.0 and later** — tag chain `v0.37.1` (2026-03-25) → `v0.38.0` (2026-05-01) → `v0.39.0` (2026-07-03) → `v0.40.0` (2026-08-20) → `v0.41.0` (2026-10-06) → `0.42.0.dev0` (HEAD `5378870`, 2026-10-20) — that have **no BlockAdapter coverage** in cache-dit. **R.6 extends the scope past diffusers**: community-hot models that ship their own modeling code and therefore never appear in a tag scan (plus one diffusers-backed family that the existing adapter rejects).
- Method: diffusers git log between upstream release tags (`--diff-filter=A` on `pipelines/`, `modular_pipelines/`, `models/transformers/`) cross-checked against `@BlockAdapterRegister.register(...)` in `cache-dit/src/cache_dit/caching/block_adapters/adapters.py`. A model counts as "supported" only when a registered adapter matches its transformer class — or a class it reuses.
- **All models — verification-only quick wins and full-adapter work — are listed in ONE unified difficulty-ordered table (R.2), easiest first.** The Type column distinguishes Verification-only (backbone class already registered; work = A/B test + CLI example + matrix entry) from Full adapter (new `BlockAdapter` needed). Within the same difficulty tier, verification-only items come first because they are cheaper.
- Difficulty assessment factors: pipeline type (regular diffusers pipeline < modular-only), block structure (uniform `ModuleList` < PatchFunctor needed < non-uniform), family reference (same-family adapter in cache-dit < analogous only < none), verification method (image PSNR/SSIM < video frames < audio < domain-specific), and interaction risks (KV-cache interplay, multi-stage pipelines, MoE routing). Business value is a separate axis — video models remain cache-dit's main workload; jump the queue when value demands it.
- Models from the v0.38+ window that are **already covered and therefore excluded**: MiniMax-H3 (v0.40, #14355), Qwen-Image 2.1 (v0.41, #14804 + modular #14976), FLUX.3 (0.42-dev, #15046), ERNIE-Image (v0.38, #13432 + modular #13498), Helios (v0.38 modular, #13216), HunyuanVideo 1.5 (v0.38 modular, #13389), LTX Video modular (v0.38, #13378), FLUX.2 Klein Inpaint / Klein-9b-kv (v0.38), SD3 modular (v0.39, #13324), AnyFlow / AnyFlow-FAR (v0.39, #13745), Cosmos3 (v0.39, #13818, incl. Cosmos3 Omni), JoyImage-Edit (v0.39, #13444), Krea 2 (v0.39, #14045), LTX-2 IC LoRA / HDR variants (v0.39, #13572), plus v0.40-era family-variant work (Cosmos3 Distilled/FP8, Wan VACE modular blockset, Krea2 modular, JoyImage Edit Plus).

Status legend: ⬜ pending · 🔄 in progress · ✅ done (move the row to R.5 with a one-line summary).

## R.3 Per-Model Integration Notes

All class names below were verified against diffusers source at HEAD `5378870`. Numbers match the R.2 rows.

### 3.1 LTX-2.5 (incl. DFR pipeline)
- Difficulty ★☆☆☆☆ (verification-only): `LTX2VideoTransformer3DModel` is covered by the `LTX` adapter (Pattern_0 + `LTX2PatchFunctor` on the `is_ltx2` path).
- Work: cache A/B test (PSNR > 30, SSIM > 0.90) on `Lightricks/LTX-2.5-Diffusers`, including the DFR pipeline variants (#14567); add CLI example; add support-matrix entry.

### 3.2 PRXPixel
- Difficulty ★★☆☆☆ (verification-only): `prx_adapter` already asserts `PRXTransformer2DModel` — the same class `PRXPixelPipeline` uses.
- ⚠️ Pixel-space pipeline (no VAE; the denoised output *is* the image): confirm the block loop and CFG handling match latent-space PRX before trusting the A/B result. Requires `transformers >= 4.57` (Qwen3-VL text encoder).
- Done (2026-10-23). Cache needed no change; CP/TP/TE-P were added because the shared class had none. Two model quirks are worth remembering: the text sequence and the RoPE must be split *outside* the block loop (`txt_in` output / `pe_embedder` ids) because PRX keeps `txt` and `pe` as loop-invariant locals, and the joint text+image key mask has to be rebuilt in the Ulysses all-to-all order. diffusers never declares `_repeated_blocks` for PRX, so regional quantization and `compile_repeated_blocks()` need the declaration cache-dit now adds.

### 3.3 Anima
- Difficulty ★★☆☆☆ (verification-only, modular): Cosmos adapter covers `CosmosTransformer3DModel`. Read [`./modular_pipeline.md`](./modular_pipeline.md) first.
- t2i → standard image metrics, fast iteration.
- Done (2026-10-23). Cache went through a thin `"Anima"` prefix adapter on the shared Cosmos `Pattern_2` branch (the registry matches pipeline class-name prefixes, so `AnimaModularPipeline` never matched `"Cosmos"`; `has_separate_cfg` derives from the modular guider's condition count). CP/TP for `CosmosTransformer3DModel` were new (`distributed/transformers/cosmos.py`). Anima quirks worth remembering: the root input is 5D latents and `padding_mask` is concatenated as an extra channel inside `patch_embed` (NOT an attention mask — no CP reorder needed), so CP is a single-point split at `transformer_blocks.0` plus a `rope` output-split (`(cos, sin)`, each `[S, D]`, split on dim 0) and a `proj_out` gather. `attn1`/`attn2` are independent `Attention` instances sharing `CosmosAttnProcessor2_0` (no img-context → no `CosmosAttention`), so one class-level dispatch patch — inert without `_cp_config` — covers both; TP needs `shard_div_attr` on BOTH attention layers and the GELU `FeedForward` keys `ff.net.0.proj` (Colwise) / `ff.net.2` (Rowwise) — there is no gate/up pair. Planner must be registered under the exact class name: the prefix `"Cosmos"` would also match `Cosmos3OmniTransformer`, which has no planner. `_repeated_blocks` is undeclared upstream, so `declare_repeated_blocks` now maps `CosmosTransformer3DModel` (fp8 regional scope: 448 layers, 0 skipped). The repo ships `modular_model_index.json`, so the CLI example needs no `modular_blocks_factory`; guidance lives in the guider component (`ModularPipeline.__call__` does not route `guidance_scale`), fixed at 4.0.

### 3.4 Echo (JoyAI-Echo)
- Difficulty ★★☆☆☆ (verification-only, modular): LTX2 backbone; modular path as in 3.3.
- ⚠️ DMD few-step sampling: few denoise steps → caching gains shrink and per-step accuracy matters more; verify per-frame PSNR/SSIM and report speedup honestly. Long video + audio output → frame-level metrics (audio checks once 3.7/3.8 land the audio methodology).
- Done (2026-10-23). `EchoModularPipeline` needs its own `"Echo"` prefix (the registry matches *pipeline* class names, so `LTX` never matched it); the adapter reuses `LTX2PatchFunctor` + `Pattern_0` verbatim — its patched forward already accepts Echo's `video_coords` / `audio_coords` / `use_cross_timestep` / `attention_kwargs`. Two gaps had to be filled: (1) Echo passes a **per-token** `audio_timestep` `(B, T_a)` where LTX-2/2.5 pass a scalar, so the shared LTX2 CP plan gained that entry (LTX-2's 1-D form is skipped by `expected_dims=2`); (2) its text encoder lives in the gated `google/gemma-3-12b-it` and `ComponentSpec` passes `subfolder=None`, which transformers cannot join onto a local path — `ExampleInitConfig.modular_load_overrides` now carries both `pretrained_model_name_or_path` and `subfolder` per-component overrides. TE-P needed a fix too: transformers 5 nests the text stack at `model.language_model.layers` (v4 used `language_model.model`), so `GemmaTensorParallelismPlanner` now unwraps generically. CP2 requires `--ulysses-anything` (audio tokens for 121 frames are odd). **Caching is not worth it**: measured Fn residual diffs are 0.46–0.70 per step (the sampler re-noises with fresh Gaussian noise at every sigma), so thr 0.12 gives 0 hits (bit-exact) and thr 0.75 gives 2.1× at SSIM 0.47. `--cpu-offload` costs 1.6× on a 72 GB card (the model fits: 68.3 GiB peak).

### 3.5 Bria Fibo 2.0
- Difficulty ★★☆☆☆: regular pipeline, uniform 2D blocks, direct same-family adapter reference, standard image verification.
- Blocks: `BriaFibo2TransformerBlock` + `BriaFibo2PerceiverResampler`; check whether the Perceiver resampler runs inside the block loop (PatchFunctor territory if so).
- Reference adapter: `briafibo_adapter` (Fibo 1.0). Start with `Fibo-2.0-edit-turbo` (fewer steps → faster verification).
- Done (2026-10-23). The adapter is a `Pattern_3` over `transformer.layers` (Z-Image lineage: blocks take `x` / `attn_mask` / `freqs_cis`, so `check_forward_pattern=False`). **Every injection layer reads its own text bundle** (`encoder_hidden_states[:, k + 1]`) inside the loop, which the collapsed cached loop cannot express → `BriaFibo2PatchFunctor` stashes bundle `k + 1` on `injection_layer_ids[k]` in a thin forward prologue (bundle 0 belongs to the Perceiver). `PatchFunctor.apply` skips an already-parallelized transformer, so both planners apply the functor themselves (idempotent) — otherwise "parallel first, cache second" silently drops the text conditioning. CP splits `x` / `freqs_cis` / `noise_mask` at *every* layer and gathers after every layer (`final_layer` slices the packed sequence with a global `image_start`, and a cached step never reaches the last block); the 2-D `attn_mask` stays full length (key-side broadcast, valid under Ulysses only → ring and UAA are rejected). TP shards attn/cross-attn heads and `feed_forward.w1/w3`+`w2`, keeping `adaLN_modulation` replicated (`chunk(4)` semantics). `Fibo-2.0-dev` runs real CFG (2 forwards/step, 30 steps) so `has_separate_cfg` derives from the `__call__` default; the distilled turbo checkpoint must pass `enable_separate_cfg=False`.

### 3.6 Motif-Video
- Difficulty ★★☆☆☆: regular pipelines (t2v + i2v, no modular), standard double→single stream blocks (Flux paradigm), 2B small model → fast iteration; no same-family adapter but the in-repo double/single pattern (`flux_adapter`) is mature; SVDQuant mapping pre-exists.
- Blocks: `MotifVideoTransformerBlock` + `MotifVideoSingleTransformerBlock` (double→single stream; cf. `flux_adapter`'s dual-block handling).
- SVDQuant `src/cache_dit/quantization/svdquant/passes.py` already maps `MotifVideoTransformerBlock` and `MotifVideoSingleTransformerBlock` — pre-work done on the quantization side.
- Verification: video — sample frames, per-frame PSNR/SSIM (precedent: Wan / LTX test flows).
- Done (2026-10-26). Real checkpoint config differs from code defaults: 12 heads × 128 (inner 1536), 12 dual + 24 single (16 encoder + **8 DDT decoder**), single-stream blocks carry a **cross-attention** (`enable_text_cross_attention_single=true`), rope_theta 10000, text 2560 (`T5Gemma2Encoder`). The forward iterates `single_transformer_blocks` through **slices** (`[:16]` encoder, `[-8:]` decoder with a full-sequence `decoder_hidden_states` clone as query stream), which collides with the `ModuleList([CachedBlocks])` replacement → `MotifVideoPatchFunctor` splits the list into `_motif_single_encoder_blocks` / `_motif_single_decoder_blocks` sub-modules and mirrors the forward; the functor also permutes the attention mask into all-to-all order (full length, hunyuan.py-style chunk+interleave) and chunks the decoder query stream under CP — no mask hook, no root split. Adapter applies the functor BEFORE reading `blocks=[...]` (constructor args evaluate before `__post_init__`), `has_separate_cfg` from `guider.num_conditions` (AdaptiveProjectedGuidance, two sequential passes per step; start/stop!=(0,1) warns). CP: single-point split at `transformer_blocks.0` + `rope` output-split + `proj_out` gather; both processors class-patched with unarmed fallback (`_CP_PATCH_ORIGINALS`), cross-attn rides Ulysses as asymmetric attention (its text mask is re-extracted from the permuted mask in rank-interleaved order); i2v CP is a known limitation (`image_embed_seq_len` is a global offset sliced on the local encoder segment). TP v1 shards the 12 dual-stream blocks only: the single-stream `attn` is `pre_only` (head-sharded output) while `cross_attn.to_out.0` is Rowwise (full width) — `attn_output + cross_output` would mix widths; fused single-stream `proj_out` split left as follow-up. TE-P: `T5Gemma2Encoder` added to `GemmaTensorParallelismPlanner` (`text_model` nesting + `T5Gemma2EncoderLayer` whitelist, vision tower untouched). VAE-P: existing `AutoencoderKLWan` planner. Measured (480×832×81f×30 steps, RTX PRO 5000): base 287.6s; cache 158.7s (PSNR 41.4 / SSIM 0.971); cache thr 0.20 148.0s; CP2 159.5s (42.3); TP2 249.6s (42.8); TP2+TE-P+VAE-P 249.4s (42.3); CP2+compile 158.4s (42.4); fp8+compile 265.0s (35.5); nvfp4+compile 264.5s (32.2); offload bit-exact (SSIM 1.000, 289–294s — negative opt on a 72 GB card). `--compile` gives ~1.02× only: `MotifVideoAttention.forward` calls `inspect.signature(processor.__call__)` per attention call (graph-break suspect); i2v at 480p/30 steps shows ghosting artifacts (official 1280×736×121×50 recommended) — integration verified bit-exact with image_embeds.

### 3.7 Stable Audio 3 — supported (2026-10-30, #1188)
- `StableAudio3DiTModel` works on 1D audio tokens; three pipeline variants (t2a / audio2audio / inpaint). Latent is `(B, 256, T)` with `T = ceil(duration*44100/4096)`; the transformer prepends 64 learned memory tokens and builds one full RoPE table for the resulting `64+T` tokens before the block loop.
- Adapter: `StableAudio3` (`Pattern_3`, `has_separate_cfg=False` — the pipeline fuses CFG into a single forward), registered **ahead of** `StableAudio` so the SA1/2 prefix cannot capture it.
- CLI: `stable_audio_3` T2A example (8 steps, duration via extra kwargs, `STABLE_AUDIO_3_DIR`); fails fast when pointed at the native `stable-audio-tools` checkpoint; `--parallel-vae` is rejected (audio VAE, ~8% of the run).
- CP: split `[memory | audio]` on block 0, split the full RoPE table on the same token axis, gather on the last block (`_cp_requires_min_bn_blocks=1`); cross attention keeps its replicated context local. Tiny parity is bit-exact for both divisible and UAA splits. Inpainting and Ring are rejected.
- TP: every fused projection is reordered into shard-part-major order so the processor's `chunk(5/2/3/2)` still yields that rank's slice of each section; only `heads` is divided (per-head QK RMSNorm stays local). Tiny parity exact.
- TE-P: `T5GemmaEncoderModel` accepted by the Gemma planner (stack at `.encoder.layers`). Offload: a leaf whose class has no `forward` (`SoftNormBottleneck`, used via `decode()`) is kept resident instead of streamed.
- Metrics: audio sampling rate falls back to `pipe.vae`; PSNR/SSIM stay image metrics — audio rows quote mel SSIM / SI-SDR (`./audio.md` §6).
- Coverage: 25 CPU tests + a two-rank parity test; GPU matrix row `Stable-Audio-3-Medium ✅/✅/✅`.

### 3.8 LongCat-AudioDiT
- Difficulty ★★★☆☆: regular pipeline, 1B model; no family reference; block IO is standard (self-attn + cross-attn + ConvNeXtV2 FFN) so the adapter itself is easy — the cost is the audio verification methodology, which is SHARED with Stable Audio 3. **Do 3.7 and 3.8 as one effort**: build the audio metrics once, integrate both.
- Blocks: `AudioDiTBlock` inside `LongCatAudioDiTTransformer` (⚠️ block class is not model-prefixed — grep `AudioDiTBlock`, not `LongCatAudio...`). ConvNeXtV2 FFN with GRN is non-standard, but block-IO caching does not care about the FFN implementation.
- 1D audio tokens, single pipeline (`LongCatAudioDiTPipeline`).
- Verified 2026-10-29 with the official 1B weights split into the diffusers layout (`meituan-longcat/LongCat-AudioDiT-1B` already keys every tensor as `transformer.* / vae.* / text_encoder.*`, so the split is a prefix strip plus a `text_encoder.encoder.embed_tokens -> shared.weight` alias). Whatever the integration, remember:
  - `blocks` is `transformer.blocks`; the block takes `hidden_states` first, returns one tensor, and the loop calls it with keywords only, so `Pattern_3` + `has_separate_cfg=True` (guidance default 4.0 → two forwards per step) needs no PatchFunctor.
  - CP: `forward` returns a dataclass, so split the **embedder outputs** (`input_embed`, `latent_embed`) with `split_output=True` instead of the transformer entry, gather at `proj_out`, drop the duration mask (it is all-True) via a thin `forward` wrapper, and rebuild the rotary table full-length + slice `[offset:offset+local]` in the processors. Cross attention queries the local shard against the **replicated** text, so it must pass `parallel_config=None` — letting Ulysses run there all-to-alls the text on every rank and the attention fails on a mask/K length mismatch. Tiny-model parity: bit-exact (divisible) / 1e-5 relative (UAA).
  - TP: the processors reshape with both `heads` **and** `inner_dim` (divide both, or `head_dim` doubles), and the QK RMSNorm must all-reduce its mean square (`_DistributedRMSNorm`), otherwise the norm spans a partial feature axis.
  - Audio acceptance: a 16-step flow + CFG 4 TTS model is **chaotic** — swapping only the attention backend moves mel PSNR to ~23 dB / SSIM 0.76 and energy-envelope correlation to 0.86, so waveform SI-SDR is not a usable signal and "PSNR > 30" only holds for cache (which perturbs few steps). Gate on log-mel PSNR/SSIM + envelope correlation + listening.
  - VAE-P is not worth implementing: the audio VAE decodes in ~2% of the run (0.014 s of 0.688 s at 10 s / 16 steps) and is a 1-D convolutional decoder.

### 3.9 Ideogram 4
- Difficulty ★★★☆☆: dual form (regular pipeline + modular); asymmetric CFG with an **independent `unconditional_transformer` instance** — precedent exists (`wan_adapter`'s Wan 2.2 MoE `transformer_2` list, `has_separate_cfg` flag), but audit how the pipeline invokes the uncond transformer before wiring.
- Blocks: `Ideogram4TransformerBlock` with MRoPE.
- Structured prompt-upsampling stage (#13860, `prompt_enhancer` component) — same pitfall class as FLUX.3 `pup` (SKILL.md pitfall 9): pop the stage for benchmarking, inject for production, and record which one the example uses.
- Verified with `ideogram-ai/ideogram-4-fp8` (2026-10-26). The regular-pipeline adapter covers both independent DiTs with `Pattern_3` and `has_separate_cfg=False`; release/summary/compile/quantize traverse both. The FP8 checkpoint needs its fused-QKV/per-row-scale conversion to BF16 while loading. Ulysses keeps `segment_ids` and the full mask global (no permutation), rejects Ring/UAA and incompatible attention backends; TP shards MHA+SwiGLU and keeps AdaLN replicated. TE-P adds the `Qwen3VLModel` wrapper; VAE-P reuses Flux2. Modular pipeline support is not included.

### 3.10 NucleusMoE-Image
- Difficulty ★★★☆☆ for **Cache**, ★★★★☆+ if CP/TP is attempted: MoE routing lives inside blocks. Block-IO caching stays valid (a skipped block skips its routing too), but CP/TP requires expert sharding — a research-level task. Recommend **Cache-only scope initially**, revisit parallelism later.
- Class: `NucleusMoEImageTransformer2DModel`.
- No family reference. HF id `NucleusAI/NucleusMoE-Image` comes from the diffusers pipeline docstring; ⚠️ not mirrored on ModelScope as of 2026-10-22 — fetch via the verified HF mirror flow (D.2 of [`./model_download.md`](./model_download.md)): `HF_ENDPOINT=https://hf-mirror.com hf download NucleusAI/NucleusMoE-Image --local_dir ./NucleusMoE-Image`.
- Done (2026-10-27). The real repo id is **`NucleusAI/Nucleus-Image`** (`NucleusMoE-Image` 307-redirects to it) and it **is** mirrored on ModelScope under that name, so the ModelScope flow works after all. Cache went in as `Pattern_2` on `transformer_blocks` with no PatchFunctor (the transformer calls blocks with keywords whose first two names match the wrapper). TP: `distributed/transformers/nucleus_moe.py` shards the attention (including `add_k_proj` / `add_v_proj` — the text KV is concatenated with the image KV), the dense + shared-expert SwiGLU FFNs, and `heads`/`inner_dim`/`inner_kv_dim`; the routed expert tables stay replicated (3-D `nn.Parameter` + `F.grouped_mm`, no DTensor strategy) so TP2 saves ~10 GiB of 51.7 GiB. **CP is deliberately not offered**: `NucleusMoELayer` derives its expert-choice capacity from the sequence length, so a sharded sequence selects a different token set (tiny-model CP2 measured rel = 0.46). Two further findings worth remembering: (a) the model is **nondeterministic run to run** (MoE `scatter_add_` / top-k ties) — repeated identical runs measure PSNR 31.6 / SSIM 0.942, so every comparison needs that noise floor next to it; (b) `--compile` is **blocked upstream** — inductor's meta check on `aten._grouped_mm` fails (`Offsets tensor must be integer (int32) tensor, but got torch.int64`) for every quantization mode, so fp8 stays eager and gains nothing. Root cause: inductor's `cumsum` decomposition drops the `dtype` kwarg (casting the input does **not** help; casting the *output* does). cache-dit now ships an opt-in fix — `CACHE_DIT_NUCLEUS_MOE_GROUPED_MM_OFFSETS_FIX=1` or `cache_dit.patch_nucleus_moe_grouped_mm_offsets()` — which unblocks compile: measured 20 steps at 1024², `--compile` 7.14s and `--compile --quantize float8_per_row` 6.51s vs 7.87s eager bf16 (compile warmup 73s / 133s). Measured (1024², 20 steps, CFG 4.0, RTX PRO 5000): base 7.87s; cache rdt 0.12 4.54s (9/20, 34.6 dB / 0.943), rdt 0.20 3.43s (12/20, 31.2 / 0.869); TP2 7.65s (31.4 / 0.891), TP2+TE-P+VAE-P 7.96s (33.1 / 0.934); fp8_per_row eager 8.70s (29.9 / 0.850); layerwise offload + async 33.4s (bit-exact within the noise floor).

### 3.11 Kandinsky 6.0
- Difficulty ★★★☆☆: heterogeneous transformer (trunk + audio decoder + SR), but the fix is a clear scoping decision (cache trunk blocks only); regular pipeline.
- Beyond the video trunk, `Kandinsky6Transformer3DModel` carries audio decoder blocks (`Kandinsky6TransformerDecoderBlock`, `Kandinsky6FusedTransformerDecoderBlock`); VSR is a separate transformer (`transformer_kandinsky6_sr.py`).
- Decide scope first: cache the main TI2VA transformer; treat SR and audio decoder as separate follow-ups.
- Reference adapter: `kandinsky5_adapter`. Start with `Kandinsky-6.0-Pro-distill-5s-Diffusers` (distilled = fewer steps → faster verification).
- Done (2026-10-27, TI2VA only). The fused block's second output stream is the **evolving audio latent**, so the adapter is `Pattern_0` on `visual_transformer_blocks` with `check_forward_pattern=False` (parameters are `vis`/`aud`); no PatchFunctor, because `forward` already calls blocks positionally. The distilled checkpoint needs `enable_separate_cfg=False` (guidance 1.0, one forward per step) — the example does that. CP (`distributed/transformers/kandinsky6.py`) shards **only the video stream**: `vis` at block 0, `vis_rope` on every block, and a gather on the **last** block's output (the audio slot is `None` in the plan) — measured **bit-exact** against a single rank. The one hard constraint is `Bn_compute_blocks >= 1` (the cached path only runs the last block inside the Bn group); the planner advertises it via `_cp_requires_min_bn_blocks` and `enable_cache` raises instead of failing later. Exactly one attention per block keeps the armed `parallel_config` (video self-attention); the rest run locally, and `av_cross_attention` (audio query, video KV) all-gathers the video activation *and* its rope. TP shards the six attentions, both GELU FFNs and the 4+4 text blocks, with every `Kandinsky6Modulation` sharded but replicated-output. Also needed: `_ContextParallelGatherHook`/`_ContextParallelSplitHook` now tolerate a `None` stream so a video-only run (`sample_audio=False`) does not crash. Measured (384×640×41 frames, 16 steps, guidance 1.0, `--cpu-offload` because the 80.7 GiB checkpoint does not fit a 71.7 GiB card): base 95.3s (repeat run bit-identical); cache rdt 0.12 79.1s (4/16, video 37.3 dB / 0.963, audio cos 0.81); rdt 0.25 63.3s (8/16, 34.5 / 0.937, cos 0.54); TP2 64.8s (1.47×, 34.0 / 0.925, cos 0.90); fp8_per_row 81.8s (33.2 / 0.936). Layerwise offload alone OOMs on a single card at this canvas — the measurements use accelerate's `--cpu-offload`. VSR (`Kandinsky6SRTransformer3DModel`) and `--compile` are untouched follow-ups.

### 3.12 MiniMax Music 3
- Difficulty ★★★☆☆: modular-only, but the MiniMax-H3 integration is the closest in-repo reference (same org, same plumbing); uniform blocks; scope is clear; audio metrics as in 3.7.
- Modular-only pipeline → read [`./modular_pipeline.md`](./modular_pipeline.md) first.
- Architecture: AR LM + 2.4B flow DiT + RVQ depth decoder; **only the flow DiT is a cache target**. Block class: `MiniMaxMusic3TransformerBlock`.

### 3.13 SANA-WM
- Difficulty ★★★★☆: camera-control cross-attention inside blocks means likely PatchFunctor surgery; two-stage main+refiner orchestration.
- Blocks: `SanaVideoMSCamCtrlBlock` — camera-control **cross-attention inside blocks** → likely PatchFunctor territory (extra inputs in the block loop).
- Two-stage pipeline: main model + LTX-2 refiner (`SanaWMLTX2Refiner`); the refiner backbone `LTX2VideoTransformer3DModel` is already covered by the `LTX` adapter.
- Reference adapters: `sana_adapter` (2D Sana) for block style, `ltxvideo_adapter` for the refiner.
- Done (2026-10-29, stage 1 + refiner). Cache turned out **cheap**: the predicted PatchFunctor surgery is not needed, because every block input except the latents (text, modulation, RoPE, camera raymaps, UCPE ray transforms, Plücker embeddings) is built once per forward *outside* the loop and the loop calls `block(*block_args)` positionally. One `"SanaWM"` registration dispatches on the block stack (`blocks` → stage 1, `transformer_blocks` → refiner) instead of relying on prefix order — both class names share the prefix, and `SanaWMLTX2Refiner*` would otherwise fall into the stage-1 branch. The block parameters are `x` / `y`, so `check_forward_pattern=False`; CFG is a single batched forward, so `has_separate_cfg=False`.
- **CP is refused by a dedicated planner** (`distributed/transformers/sana_wm.py`): both attention branches are recurrences along the temporal axis (bidirectional gated delta rule, camera branch in UCPE ray space) and `GLUMBConvTemp` mixes frames again, so a sequence shard needs per-frame state/halo exchange, which Ulysses/Ring do not provide. vllm-omni pins `skip_sequence_parallel=True` and sglang raises for `sp_degree != 1`; the planner raises `NotImplementedError` with that explanation instead of letting the registry fail generically.
- **TP is a memory optimization, not a speedup**: `attn.qkv` is one fused `Linear(C, 3C)` reshaped as `(B, N, 3, heads, dim)`, Q/K RMSNorm runs over the full channel axis and the short convolution reshapes back with `channels = x.shape[-1]`, so activations must stay full width — the plan shards weights with `output_layouts=Replicate()` (PRX recipe) for `qkv`/`output_gate`/`beta_proj`/`gate_proj`/camera projections/`cross_attn`, and `RowwiseParallel(input_layouts=Replicate())` for the output projections. `mlp` is `Conv2d` end to end (≈half the block GEMM) and `final_layer.linear` would scramble the patch layout, so both stay replicated. Measured TP2 = 6.61s vs 5.56s single card at 352×640×25f×30 steps (PSNR 38.0 / SSIM 0.976), i.e. it costs latency and saves weights.
- Stage 2 needs `SanaWMRefinerPatchFunctor`: after the block list collapses, upstream's `kv_cache.get(i)` would hand every layer layer 0's slot, and the two KV-writing passes (`capture_pre_rope`, `inject_and_capture_post_rope`) must not be skipped. The functor (a) binds each block's `forward` to resolve the shared container into its own layer slice, (b) replays the original blocks on any `kv_cache_mode` pass, (c) refreshes the cache context through `force_refresh_step_hint` at each autoregressive chunk boundary (the geometry marker trick does not work here — every chunk has identical token counts), and (d) checks `len(kv_cache)` against the real block count.
- Cache quality depends strongly on **clip length**, not canvas size: the GDN recurrence carries the per-step approximation across the 21 latent frames of a 161-frame clip. Measured on RTX PRO 5000 (bf16, same seed): 352×640×25f×30 steps 5.56s → 2.52s (rdt 0.10, 19/30 cached) at PSNR 29.1 / SSIM 0.944; 704×1280×25f×60 steps 41.0s → 15.3s (rdt 0.10, 41/60) at 23.9 / 0.910; 704×1280×161f×60 steps 244.7s → 89.1s (rdt 0.10, 41/60) at 14.0 / 0.726 (and at rdt 0.03, 31/60, 127.2s, 16.4 / 0.779). Long camera-motion clips are therefore a documented quality/speed trade-off, not a bug.
- Also measured: `--compile` works (block-level path finds `SanaVideoMSCamCtrlBlock` through the upstream `_repeated_blocks`; the GDN chunk scan does not graph-break the steady state), fp8 per-row + compile 2.80s at 30.3 / 0.952, layerwise offload **bit-exact** (transformer-only: sync 9.18s, async 7.77s vs 5.56s — negative on a 72 GB card), TP2+TE-P 6.65s and TP2+VAE-P 6.60s (Gemma2 / `AutoencoderKLLTX2Video` planners already existed). W4A4 was not measurable in the dev container: the SVDQuant extension is not built there and torchao NVFP4 fails on the model's `expand`/`per_tensor_scale` paths.

### 3.14 Wan-Animate-2
- Done (2026-10-29, base + distilled). Adapter `WanAnimate2` (registered **before** `Wan`), `ForwardPattern.Pattern_3`, `blocks=transformer.blocks` (not `transformer_blocks`), `has_separate_cfg` from `guider.num_conditions`; the "Wan" entry had to be **removed from `_predefined_adapters_has_separate_cfg`**, otherwise the prefix fallback flips the distilled checkpoint (guidance 1.0, one forward per step) back to two-pass bookkeeping and halves the step count.
- `WanAnimate2PatchFunctor` (`caching/patch_functors/functor_wan_animate_2.py`) is mandatory, same failure mode as Qwen-Image 2.1: cache-dit's wrapper drives every block with one shared kwargs set, so upstream's `kv_cache.get(idx)` would hand layer 0's slice to all 40 layers (colour noise, no crash) and `if is_uncondtion and idx == 9: continue` would run one extra layer. Both are pushed into the block (`block._idx`, `is_uncondtion` forwarded as a block kwarg).
- **The `extract` pass must bypass the cached wrapper**: it runs once *per segment* (not once per request) to fill `WanAnimate2KVCache` with pre-RoPE K/V. The copied forward iterates `self._wan_animate2_blocks` (tuple saved at patch time) whenever `kv_cache_mode == "extract"`, so every layer writes its slot and `mark_step_begin` never sees the pass (which would otherwise flip the cond/uncond parity).
- Cross-segment step counting is left continuous; the segment-start residual is far from the previous segment's buffer, so it misses by default. Thresholds above ~0.3 can reuse a stale residual across the segment boundary — keep `--max-warmup-steps` >= 1 segment worth of steps if that matters.
- CP: `WanAnimate2ContextParallelismPlanner` shards the token sequence in the forward and runs **full-sequence attention with head-sharded K/V** (`_All2AllComm`), because the flex `BlockMask` indexes the full `[generation | reference]` packed buffer. Ring and `ulysses_anything` raise. The flex branch must dispatch through **diffusers'** `dispatch_attention_fn` (`cache-dit`'s registry has no flex backend); `parallel_config=None` everywhere since the comm is explicit. Two traps found while wiring: the gathered sequence is padded, so (a) trim to `frames * h * w` before the output all-to-all, and (b) store only the unpadded rows into the K/V cache.
- TP: `shard_div_attr(self_attn/cross_attn, "heads")`, Colwise `to_q/to_k/to_v`, Rowwise `to_out.0`, `ffn.0`/`ffn.2`, and `DistributedRMSNorm.from_rmsnorm` (the **`wan.py` version with all-reduce**; `anyflow.py`'s variant has none) because `norm_q/norm_k/norm_added_k` normalize over the full 5120-wide dim before the head unflatten. Import it lazily inside the planner — a module-level `from .wan import ...` registers the "Wan" planner first and the prefix lookup then picks it.
- Offload: upstream derives the RoPE device from `patch_embedding.weight`; layerwise offload parks that module on CPU, so the copied forward uses the latents' device instead.
- ⚠️ `--layerwise-offload` failed **once** (twice back-to-back, 2026-10-29 14:32) with `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid argument` inside `offload/layerwise.py::_prepare_async_target` → `cpu_tensor.pin_memory()`. **It is not a model or weights problem and it is not reproducible**: the same command now pins the whole pipeline (text_encoder 11.4 GiB → image_encoder → vae → transformer, ~43 GiB pinned, `Inference Time 16.06 s` at 2 steps / `48.92 s` at 8 steps). Ruled out by probe: read-only safetensors mmap aliases (`get_tensor` and zero-copy `get_slice` both pin fine), synthetic `PROT_READ` mmap buffers, 0-element / non-contiguous / already-pinned tensors, all 1303 transformer CPU tensors, a 40 GiB cumulative pinned ceiling (host has 2.2 TB RAM), `RLIMIT_MEMLOCK`, and `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=pinned_use_cuda_host_register`. The failures sit immediately after an uncompiled 480x384 run was OOM-killed on the same GPU and everything from 14:37 on works, so the remaining hypothesis is a transient driver-side host-registration failure (`cudaHostAlloc`/`cudaHostRegister` returning `cudaErrorInvalidValue`); dmesg shows no Xid at that time. Fixed in `ed8d589`: `pin_memory()` is only a staging optimisation, so `offload/layerwise.py::_pinned_cpu_mirror` now degrades to pageable memory on a refused pin (both the CPU-source and the CUDA-source `empty_like(pin_memory=True)` paths), warns once with module/tensor/dtype/size, keeps host OOM fatal, and is covered by `tests/quantization/test_layerwise_offload.py::test_layerwise_cpu_offload_falls_back_to_pageable_memory` (sync + bucketed async) plus `..._when_pinned_allocation_fails`.
- Quality notes: the base checkpoint is a 40-step CFG model, 8 steps produces a barely-converged sample (visually headless cat) so PSNR/SSIM comparisons at 8 steps are chaotic; cache 0.12 on 40 steps gives 24/40 cached at 2.37x (PSNR 32.6 / SSIM 0.886). flex attention **must** be compiled for large canvases — uncompiled it materialises the score matrix and OOMs at 480x384 (65 GiB allocated before a final 8.9 GiB request).
- **Why `--compile` is 4.14x here (measured, not attention)**: one 3-forward request at 208x368 profiled by kernel class gives eager 2.11 s GEMM / 2.56 s elementwise / 0.64 s copy / 0.31 s attention (5.81 s wall) vs compiled 1.50 / 0.26 / 0.35 / 0.20 (2.28 s wall). The whole gain is the elementwise bucket collapsing (~85k device events per request eager vs ~58k compiled: RoPE, AdaLN `modulation`, mask `where`, 128-aligned K/V packing with zeros/scatter/cat, norms, GELU); attention is 6% -> 9% and compiling flex is worth a few percent at most. GEMM is already efficient eager (41.3 TFLOP GEMM + 7.2 TFLOP attention per forward = 85%/15%), so the honest framing is "eager is fusion-bound", not "flex is slow". Do not repeat the guess that flex compile is the driver — measure the class split with `torch.profiler` key_averages filtered to raw device kernels (skip `aten::*`/`cuda*` keys, they double count) and drop `Command Buffer Full`.
- SVDQuant: `fused_gelu_mlp` matches the generic `Sequential(Linear, GELU, Linear)` so no new mapping is needed; nvfp4 r64 needs `--quantize-exclude-layers time_embedding.0 time_embedding.2 time_projection.1` (fp32 linears from `_keep_in_fp32_modules`) and works on sm_120.
- CLI: `ExampleType.ANIMATE` + `--driving-video-path` / `--driving-video-fps`; the modular output is PIL frames via `output_type="pil"` and `output="videos"` (a bare value, not a dict) — `run()` now normalises list/array/`.frames` shapes.

- Architecture: beat/lyrics encoders + flow DiT + RVQ decoder; **scope: cache the flow DiT only**.

### 3.16 RFD4-Proteina
- Difficulty ★★★★★: non-uniform structure that `BlockAdapter`'s flat `ModuleList` assumption may not hold; domain-specific verification.
- `RFD4ProteinaTransformer` = trunk layers (`RFD4ProteinaTrunkLayer`) + pair modules (`RFD4ProteinaPairBuilder`, triangle multiplication, pair transition) — **NOT a uniform repeated-block DiT**. `BlockAdapter` assumes a flat homogeneous `ModuleList`; this model likely needs a custom PatchFunctor or a different integration approach entirely.
- Schedule last; budget extra design time. Outputs are protein structures — correctness verification needs domain-appropriate checks, not PSNR/SSIM.

## R.4 Out of Scope — In diffusers v0.38/0.39 but Excluded from cache-dit

Documented so future refreshes do not re-add them:

- **LLaDA2** (v0.38.0, #13226, 2026-03-25) and **DiffusionGemma** (v0.39.0, #13986, 2026-06-25): discrete-diffusion text LMs (masked-token remasking, not continuous flow matching). Block caching exploits the temporal smoothness of continuous DiT trajectories; discrete remasking breaks that assumption. Excluded unless a discrete-diffusion caching strategy is ever designed.
- **DreamLite** (v0.39.0, #13815, 2026-06-12): UNet backbone (`unets/unet_dreamlite.py`) with only an auxiliary 2D transformer — cache-dit is a DiT engine, and the auxiliary transformer is not the compute bottleneck. Out of scope.

Verified on RTX PRO 5000 (1024², 30 steps, CFG 4.0): baseline 8.21s, cache rdt0.12 4.41s (15/30 cached, 33.4 dB / 0.927), CP2 6.85s (40.9 / 0.983), TP2 7.44s (40.8 / 0.983), fp8+compile 4.20s (30.8 dB / 0.815 — SSIM is the visible cost, keep for speed-critical runs only), svdq nvfp4+compile 4.13s (30.0 dB / 0.651 — coherent image, fur/texture softening only, no garbling; visual-checked), layerwise offload bit-exact (inf / 1.000); TE-P (Qwen3) TP2+text 7.53s (36.5 / 0.962) and VAE-P (QwenImage VAE) TP2+vae 7.42s (40.7 / 0.981) run as-is. ## R.6 Community-Hot Models Without a diffusers Implementation

R.2 is built from a diffusers tag scan. This section covers the other half of the backlog: models that are hot in the community but **ship their own modeling code and have never landed in diffusers**, so no tag scan will surface them and the R.2 workflow (diffusers class names, upstream `_repeated_blocks`, upstream tests) does not apply. Integration cost is structurally higher — cache-dit's adapters are written against diffusers attribute names, so each of these needs either a third-party pipeline wrapper (precedent: `MOSSImageTransformer`, `BooguImageTransformer2DModel`, `LongCatVideoTransformer3DModel`) or a transformer-class registration. **Before planning any row in this section, read [`./custom_models.md`](./custom_models.md)**: it carries the vendor-vs-depend decision and the contracts that a non-diffusers pipeline/transformer must preserve.

The 2026-10-28 batch (SANA-Video 2.0, LongLive 2.0, HY-Nomas, Hunyuan3D 2, Kandinsky 6 VSR, LingBot-World v1) was cross-checked against SGLang Diffusion's model catalog, currently the widest third-party diffusion inventory — refresh R.6 the same way.

The R.2 difficulty scale applies unchanged. Two properties dominate the estimate: whether the block stack is a uniform `ModuleList`, and whether the model keeps a **cross-step KV cache** — the latter decides whether block-level skipping is legal at all, not merely how much work it is.

### 6.1 Already in diffusers — coverage gaps

- **SANA-Video-2B** (T2V + I2V), ★☆☆☆☆, `SanaVideoTransformer3DModel` (v0.41): the stack is `transformer_blocks` with the `Pattern_3` contract, i.e. exactly what `sana_adapter` already handles — only the `_relaxed_assert` allow-list rejects the class, so a diffusers pipeline trips `AssertionError` inside `enable_cache`. Work = add the class to the allow-list (or register a `SanaVideo` prefix) + cache A/B + CLI example + matrix row. Weights: [Efficient-Large-Model/SANA-Video_2B_480p_diffusers](https://huggingface.co/Efficient-Large-Model/SANA-Video_2B_480p_diffusers). Status: ⬜
  Do not confuse it with **SANA-WM** (R.2 #13), whose stack is named `blocks` and which needs its own adapter.
- **Kandinsky 6 VSR**, ★★★☆☆, `Kandinsky6SRTransformer3DModel` (`transformer_kandinsky6_sr.py`): the TI2VA trunk is already covered by the `Kandinsky6` adapter, but the video-super-resolution stage is a **separate transformer** (`Kandinsky6SRTransformerBlock`, own stack) that the adapter cannot reach — and because the `"Kandinsky6"` prefix also matches the SR class, the SR transformer is routed into `kandinsky6_adapter`, which then looks for `visual_transformer_blocks`. Work = a dedicated `Kandinsky6SR` prefix + adapter + A/B. ⚠️ the shipped checkpoint is `distilled2steps`, so the skip budget is tiny: treat this as a correctness exercise, not a speedup one. Weights: [kandinskylab/Kandinsky-6.0-VSR-distilled2steps-5s-Diffusers](https://huggingface.co/kandinskylab/Kandinsky-6.0-VSR-distilled2steps-5s-Diffusers). Status: ⬜

### 6.3 Excluded from R.6

- **Stable-Diffusion-XL** — UNet backbone (`SDXLUNet2DConditionModel`), not a DiT; same exclusion as DreamLite in R.4.
- **DreamZero-DROID** — robot action-policy world model (`CausalWanModel` over action chunks), not an image/video generation target.
- **LLaDA-Image / -Turbo** (`inclusionAI/LLaDA-Image`, `LLaDAImageTransformer2DModel`, `layers`) — discrete-diffusion image model (SigVQ tokens + masked remasking), not continuous flow matching. Same reasoning as the LLaDA2 exclusion in R.4: block caching exploits temporal smoothness along a continuous denoise trajectory, which token remasking does not have.

## R.7 Unified Support Priority — Community Task Value × Cache-DiT Fit

This is the queue for choosing the next integration; R.2 and R.6 remain ordered by implementation difficulty. It covers every model or variant still marked pending, partially done, or unverified on 2026-10-31. Completed scopes are not listed again: for example, only LingBot-Video MoE appears here, not the completed dense variant, and only Kandinsky 6 VSR appears, not the completed TI2VA trunk.

Scores are editorial 1–5 prioritization aids, not benchmark results:

- **Community**: breadth and likely demand of the task. General video, interactive/world models, avatars, and broadly used image/editing families rank above narrower audio, restoration, 3D, and scientific tasks.
- **Fit**: how much of Cache-DiT can plausibly help — continuous multi-step DiT blocks, legal block skipping, useful CP/TP/offload/quantization/compile, and practical acceptance metrics. Cross-step KV, few-step distillation, MoE routing, non-uniform stacks, and domain-specific validation lower the score.
- Rows are ordered by both axes, then by currently reusable integrations and unblock value. A high rank is **not** a promised DBCache speedup: the first residual-diff/cache A/B is still mandatory. P0 = next, P1 = high, P2 = medium, P3 = low.

| Rank | Model / pending scope | Community | Fit | Tier | Rationale and main caveat |
|---:|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|---|
| 1 | MAGI-2-preview | 5 | 5 | P0 | General T2VA + I2VA with a `Pattern_3` stack and no documented cross-step KV; best value/risk ratio. Keep pre/post adapters outside the cached stack. |
| 2 | LongLive 2.0 (5B) | 5 | 4 | P0 | Interactive long video makes CP/offload valuable, and CausVid-Wan plus Wan-Animate-2 now provide concrete chunk-KV recipes. Cache must be chunk-aware; do not assume a DMD student benefits from DBCache. |
| 3 | LongCat-Video-Avatar-1.5 | 5 | 4 | P0 | High-demand audio-driven avatar video with uniform blocks, an external audio projection, and a manually wired non-avatar sibling to reuse. |
| 4 | SANA-Video-2B | 4 | 5 | P0 | Cheapest video coverage gap: the existing SANA `Pattern_3` path should only need registration plus the full A/B matrix. High fit, but less strategic novelty than the three rows above. |
| 5 | HY-Nomas | 4 | 4 | P1 | Camera-controlled video is a strong Cache-DiT workload; `double_blocks` are cacheable, but the per-step camera attention likely needs a PatchFunctor. |
| 6 | MOVA 360p / 720p | 4 | 4 | P1 | Reuse the Wan-shaped video stack while keeping the separate audio DiT out of scope. Verify that the accidental `"Wan"` prefix match is made explicit and safe. |
| 7 | VDN-H3 | 4 | 4 | P1 | MiniMax-H3 integration is already available; verify VDN frame-alpha/gating, block I/O, and `has_separate_cfg=False` before claiming family coverage. |
| 8 | MiniMax Music 3 | 4 | 4 | P1 | Broad music task with a clear target: cache only the 2.4B flow DiT and leave AR LM/RVQ depth decoding outside. Modular plumbing and audio metrics are the main costs. |
| 9 | BAGEL-7B-MoT | 5 | 3 | P1 | Popular T2I/edit family and unlocks Lance, but `NaiveCache` plus cond/uncond accounting requires a custom `CachedAdapter`, not a plain block wrapper. |
| 10 | LingBot-World v1 fast / v2 causal-fast | 5 | 3 | P1 | Interactive world generation is strategically valuable; causal chunk KV and streaming step accounting must be proven before any block skipping is enabled. |
| 11 | HunyuanImage3.0 | 5 | 3 | P1 | High-value image generation with `Pattern_4` block I/O; `ImageKVCacheManager` desynchronization is the go/no-go risk. |
| 12 | MammothModa2-Preview | 3 | 4 | P2 | Lumina-style `layers` / `Pattern_3` are a good technical fit for T2I/edit. Keep all three Q-Former refiners outside the cached loop. |
| 13 | Cosmos3 sim / multiview / dreams variants | 3 | 4 | P2 | The existing Cosmos3 adapter should be reusable, but each variant's per-step lidar/rig/action conditioning needs A/B verification; tasks are narrower than general video. |
| 14 | Lance | 4 | 3 | P2 | Schedule immediately after BAGEL: the `layers` stack and KV design are inherited, while the Qwen2.5-VL vision tower and RoPE still need separate validation. |
| 15 | SenseNova-U1 / U1.5 (incl. A3B-MoE) | 4 | 3 | P2 | Cache only the denoise-side stack; the AR trunk and flash/paged KV must remain synchronized, with extra MoE risk for A3B. |
| 16 | ABot-World-0.5B | 4 | 3 | P2 | Relevant causal world-model task and a regular `blocks` stack, but per-chunk KV makes chunk-boundary correctness more important than raw cache hits. |
| 17 | WanCausalDMD | 4 | 3 | P2 | Wan/CausVid code and tests are reusable, but few-step sampling plus cross-chunk KV caps the likely DBCache upside; CP/offload may be the stronger motivation. |
| 18 | ACE-Step 1.5 | 4 | 3 | P2 | Valuable music family, but mixed block types and diffusers' own `CacheMixin` make cache ownership and validation substantially harder than MiniMax Music 3. |
| 19 | Hunyuan3D 2 | 4 | 3 | P2 | Flux-like single-stream blocks are familiar, and text/image-to-3D is useful; geometry-specific acceptance metrics, not the adapter, are the dominant cost. |
| 20 | LingBot-Video MoE 30B-A3B | 4 | 2 | P3 | Valuable large video variant, but the dense integration deliberately dropped the MoE router/expert kernels. MoE execution and CP/TP strategy are research work, not a variant checkbox. |
| 21 | Kandinsky 6 VSR | 3 | 2 | P3 | Needs a dedicated SR adapter and prefix despite TI2VA support; the released two-step checkpoint leaves very little block-skip budget. |
| 22 | SeedVR2-3B | 3 | 2 | P3 | Useful restoration task, but one-pass few-step inference and multi-scale NaDiT limit cache payoff; schedule only for a concrete product need. |
| 23 | RFD4-Proteina | 2 | 1 | P3 | Non-uniform trunk/pair structure does not fit a flat `BlockAdapter`, and protein-structure correctness needs domain-specific validation. Keep last among plausible custom integrations. |

### 7.1 Unsupported but Currently Excluded

These entries are also unsupported, ordered by their proximity to a possible future Cache-DiT scope. They are **not** an implementation queue and should not be re-added without resolving the stated structural mismatch.

| Order | Model | Why it is excluded now |
|---:|---|---|
| E1 | NextStep-1.1 | AR LM + flow head sees one step per token block; there is no long, smooth denoise trajectory for DBCache to exploit. Reconsider only with a discrete/AR caching design. |
| E2 | LLaDA-Image / -Turbo | Discrete SigVQ diffusion with masked remasking, not continuous flow matching; the block-cache premise does not hold. |
| E3 | DiffusionGemma | Discrete-diffusion text LM with masked-token remasking, outside the continuous DiT cache design. |
| E4 | LLaDA2 | Same discrete-remasking mismatch as DiffusionGemma, with no image/video DiT target to justify a separate path. |
| E5 | Stable-Diffusion-XL | UNet backbone (`SDXLUNet2DConditionModel`), not a DiT. |
| E6 | DreamLite | UNet backbone; the auxiliary transformer is not the compute bottleneck, so a DiT-only integration misses the target. |
| E7 | DreamZero-DROID | Robot action-policy world model rather than an image/video generation target. |

## R.8 How to Refresh This List

Run on each new diffusers release (paths relative to `/workspace/dev/vipshop/diffusers` and `/workspace/dev/vipshop/cache-dit`):

```bash
# 1. Discover new release tags from upstream (the local fork lags behind on tags)
git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers.git | grep -E "refs/tags/v[0-9.]+$" | sort -V

# 2. Fetch the boundary tags you want to compare (the v0.37.1..0.41 chain was fetched
#    in the 2026-10-22 passes as upstream-v0.37.1/38/39/40/41)
git fetch --no-tags https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers.git \
  refs/tags/v0.42.0:refs/tags/upstream-v0.42.0 \
  refs/tags/v0.43.0:refs/tags/upstream-v0.43.0

# 3. List newly added pipelines / transformers between the tags.
#    ⚠️ modular-only models live under modular_pipelines/ — do not scan pipelines/ only.
git --no-pager log upstream-v0.42.0..upstream-v0.43.0 --diff-filter=A \
  --pretty=format:"COMMIT %h %ad %s" --date=short \
  -- src/diffusers/pipelines src/diffusers/modular_pipelines src/diffusers/models/transformers

# 4. Supported side: the authoritative list of registered adapters
grep -n "BlockAdapterRegister.register" src/cache_dit/caching/block_adapters/adapters.py
```

Also check for models that **reuse** an already-registered backbone class (like LTX-2.5 / PRXPixel / Anima / Echo above) — they only need verification, not an adapter. New rows must be inserted into R.2 at the position their difficulty dictates, and R.3 renumbered accordingly.

### 8.1 Non-diffusers models (R.6)

There is no release tag to diff. Triage each community candidate with four questions, in this order:

1. **Does it ship its own `modeling_*` / `transformer_*.py`?** If yes, cache-dit needs a pipeline wrapper or a transformer-class registration before any adapter work starts (precedent: MOSS-Image, Boogu-Image, LongCat-Video).
2. **What is the block `ModuleList` attribute called, and what is the block `forward()` contract?** `transformer_blocks` / `layers` / `blocks` are all in use; the contract decides `ForwardPattern` (0/2/3/4).
3. **Does it keep a cross-step KV cache (or a causal chunk KV)?** This is the go/no-go: a plain `BlockAdapter` is only valid when skipping blocks cannot desync that cache, otherwise a custom `CachedAdapter` is required.
4. **Is there a same-family adapter to reuse?** Family reuse (Z-Image for Ming-Image, Wan for S2V/CausVid, BAGEL for Lance, MiniMax-H3 for TaoMate) is the difference between ★★ and ★★★★.

Subclassing an already-registered backbone is the cheapest case — verify the block stack is inherited unchanged, add the new class name to the registry (prefix or allow-list), then run the standard A/B.
